title: Regulatory Essentials for All Staff
summary: An eight-module foundation programme giving all staff a practical understanding of regulation, conduct, financial crime awareness and their own responsibilities.
intro: This training programme equips all staff in a regulated firm with a clear understanding of why regulation matters, the firm's key obligations and their own responsibilities for conduct, customers and financial crime prevention.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give staff at every level a practical understanding of the regulatory obligations that shape their day-to-day work and the reasons behind them. Participants leave able to recognise risks, apply the firm's policies and speak up or escalate when something looks wrong.
sections.What It Covers: Why regulation matters, the firm's regulatory obligations, treating customers fairly, financial crime awareness, sanctions, market abuse awareness, conflicts of interest and gifts, data protection and information security, speaking up, and conduct and personal accountability.
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners as part of induction
Front-office, operations, technology and support staff who need a regulatory grounding
Line managers responsible for embedding good conduct in their teams
Learning Objectives: Explain why financial services are regulated and the firm's key obligations
Apply the principles of fair treatment of customers in everyday work
Recognise financial crime, sanctions and market abuse red flags and escalate them
Identify and manage conflicts of interest, gifts and hospitality
Protect personal and confidential information and report incidents
Speak up confidently and meet the conduct standards expected of all staff
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about ninety minutes each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day induction programme or as a series of short sessions across the year. Modules combine short briefings with real-world examples and scenario questions, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's policies and business.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of regulation is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners and as annual refresher training.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)

modules.title: Why Regulation Matters and the Firm's Obligations
modules.summary: Why financial services are regulated, what the authority expects of the firm, and how every member of staff contributes to meeting those obligations.
objectives: Explain why financial services are regulated and what regulation aims to achieve
Describe the firm's key regulatory obligations and the role of the authority
Recognise how individual actions affect the firm's regulatory standing
syllabus: Objectives of regulation: consumer protection, market integrity and stability
The firm's licence, permissions and the authority's supervisory approach
The three lines of defence and where each role fits
Consequences of failure for customers, the firm and individuals

modules.title: Treating Customers Fairly
modules.summary: What fair treatment of customers means day to day, from clear communications to complaints and the needs of vulnerable customers.
objectives: Explain the principles of fair treatment and good customer outcomes
Recognise the signs of customer vulnerability and respond appropriately
Identify and escalate complaints and potential customer harm
syllabus: Fair, clear and not misleading communications
Suitable products, fair value and avoiding mis-selling
Vulnerable customers and reasonable adjustments
Recognising and handling complaints

modules.title: Financial Crime Awareness
modules.summary: How criminals use financial firms to launder money and finance terrorism, the red flags staff should recognise, and how to report suspicions without tipping off.
objectives: Explain money laundering, terrorist financing and fraud in plain terms
Recognise common red flags in customers and transactions
Report suspicions internally and avoid tipping off
syllabus: The stages of money laundering and common typologies
Customer due diligence and why it matters
Red flags and internal suspicious activity reporting
Fraud, scams and bribery and corruption risks

modules.title: Sanctions and Market Abuse Awareness
modules.summary: The basics of financial sanctions and market abuse: what they prohibit, how breaches happen and what staff must do to prevent and report them.
objectives: Explain what financial sanctions are and how firms comply with them
Recognise insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation
Identify when to escalate a potential sanctions or market abuse concern
syllabus: Sanctions regimes, asset freezes and screening
Evasion techniques and sanctions red flags
Inside information, insider lists and personal account dealing
Market manipulation and suspicious transaction reporting

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest, Gifts and Hospitality
modules.summary: How conflicts of interest arise in everyday work, how the firm identifies and manages them, and the rules on gifts, hospitality and outside interests.
objectives: Identify actual and potential conflicts of interest
Apply the firm's gifts, hospitality and outside interests rules
Record and escalate conflicts appropriately
syllabus: What a conflict of interest is and why it matters
Conflicts between the firm, its staff and its customers
Gifts, hospitality, inducements and registers
Outside business interests and personal relationships

modules.title: Data Protection and Information Security
modules.summary: Staff responsibilities for protecting personal and confidential information, recognising cyber threats and reporting incidents promptly.
objectives: Apply data protection principles to everyday handling of information
Recognise phishing, social engineering and other cyber threats
Report data breaches and security incidents promptly
syllabus: Personal data, confidentiality and need-to-know
Secure handling, sharing, retention and disposal of information
Phishing, social engineering and safe use of devices and AI tools
Incident and breach reporting

modules.title: Speaking Up
modules.summary: Why speaking up protects customers and the firm, how to raise concerns through internal and external channels, and the protections available to those who do.
objectives: Explain why speaking up matters to the firm and its supervisors
Identify the channels for raising concerns, including whistleblowing
Describe the protections against victimisation for those who speak up
syllabus: Culture, psychological safety and the cost of silence
Internal escalation routes and whistleblowing arrangements
Confidentiality, anonymity and protection from detriment
Reporting directly to the authority

modules.title: Conduct and Personal Accountability
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around the conduct standards that apply to all staff and the personal consequences of misconduct, closing with practical scenarios.
objectives: Explain the conduct standards expected of all staff
Recognise the personal consequences of misconduct
Apply the programme to realistic workplace scenarios
syllabus: Conduct rules: integrity, skill, care and diligence and openness with the authority
Fitness and propriety and the personal impact of breaches
Record-keeping, attestations and annual training
Workshop: what would you do? Everyday regulatory dilemmas

related.title: Cyber, Data and Resilience Essentials
related.summary: A six-module foundation programme giving all staff the practical habits to resist cyber attacks, protect data, use AI tools safely and report incidents.

related.title: Financial Crime Essentials for All Staff
related.summary: An eight-module foundation programme helping all staff recognise financial crime red flags, follow the firm's controls and report suspicions without tipping off.

related.title: Sustainable Finance Essentials
related.summary: A six-module foundation programme giving all staff a practical grounding in ESG, climate risk, sustainable products and avoiding greenwashing.
